content.overview: Protected culture changes the crop environment rather than removing environmental risk. Greenhouses and high tunnels can trap heat and humidity, alter airflow, exclude rainfall and change irrigation demand, so ventilation and monitoring become central management tasks.

vocabulary.definition: Crop production under structures such as greenhouses or high tunnels that modify the environment.
Exchange of internal and external air used to manage heat, humidity and gas conditions.
Liquid water formed when moist air contacts a surface below its dew point.

sections.title: Structures change heat balance
sections.body: Solar radiation can raise protected-culture temperature rapidly above outdoor air temperature. Ventilation, shading and crop water status should be considered together during warm periods.

sections.title: Humidity can accumulate
sections.body: Plants release water vapor while the structure restricts free air exchange. High humidity and condensation can persist when ventilation is insufficient, increasing disease-favorable conditions.

sections.title: Irrigation becomes more controlled
sections.body: Because rainfall may be excluded, the crop depends more completely on the installed irrigation system. Distribution, water quality and monitoring therefore become critical.

workedExamples: A cool morning can still produce rapid tunnel heating after sunrise; use internal sensors rather than outdoor temperature alone.
If condensation forms nightly, review humidity, ventilation timing and plant density rather than treating it only as a surface-cleaning issue.
commonMistakes: Using outdoor weather readings as if they equal greenhouse conditions.
Closing ventilation too long to preserve heat without checking humidity.
Assuming protected culture eliminates disease risk.
content.practicalApplication: Log internal and external temperature/RH, note ventilation position, irrigation timing and condensation. Compare conditions through the day and night to identify when the structure creates excessive heat or humidity.
content.summary: Protected culture is active climate management. Heat, humidity, ventilation and irrigation must be measured inside the structure because the crop no longer experiences outdoor conditions directly.
